summary: Moot and unresolvable under master 1.293x. Its headline target (sliding decode_1) no longer calls FA3 at all since sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate landed. On the remaining shapes FA3 still compiles its Varlen template because cache_seqlens (seqused_k) is passed, so dropping cu_seqlens_q saves at most some per-CTA offset arithmetic. That is far below the ~1.5-2.5% per-shape run-to-run drift, and attention has only 2 checks left.
justification: A: The claimed mechanism is that varlen-q makes FA3 take a 'varlen-q code path (cu_seqlens reads, per-request offset arithmetic, varlen tile scheduler)'. That is mostly wrong for this call. In FA3 (hopper flash_api), is_varlen is true when any of cu_seqlens_q, cu_seqlens_k, seqused_q, seqused_k or leftpad_k is set. kernel_fn always passes cache_seqlens, which is seqused_k, so the Varlen kernel instantiation, the varlen tile scheduler and prepare_varlen_num_blocks (when no scheduler_metadata is given) all stay in place. The only removed work is one int32 load of cu_seqlens_q[b], [b+1] per CTA in place of b*seqlen_q. That is nanoseconds inside a 10-13 us FA3 kernel, and the loads are L2-resident. The profile in FINDINGS shows no varlen-q-specific kernel to remove. The prepare_varlen_num_blocks rows (1.7-3.5 us) come from seqused_k plus metadata=None on the paired and sliding paths, and this change does not touch them. Shape coverage: (1) sliding decode_1, the 'launch-bound 21 us' shape the hypothesis leads with, now routes to _sliding_forward (13.1 us, no FA3), so its expected 'faster' is moot. (2) Sliding decode_16/32 (20.9/25.0 us, FA3 9.9/13.3 us) are the only real targets, and any plausible gain is <<1% per shape. (3) Full decode_1 (unpaired, judge metadata) and full decode_16/32 (paired, metadata=None) are FA3-bound, and the expected 'flat' is right. The verify 'flat' is right too. The hypothesis itself says 'Likely outcome: inside the CI on every shape'. Weakest link: the premise that cu_seqlens_q=None leaves the varlen path. With seqused_k set, it does not.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: moves sliding batch-1 decode off FA3 entirely, which removes the hypothesis's lead shape. Any 'sliding decode_1' movement in the run would be drift, not this change.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing + paired-heads-launch-cleanup(-ab-tune-batch-gate): full decode at batch>1 now calls FA3 on a paired [tokens, hq, 128] q with scheduler_metadata=None. The change would also reshape that q to [B,1,hq,128], a different call geometry from the one the hypothesis reasoned about. Full decode_1 stays unpaired with the judge's metadata, which was built with cu_seqlens_q, so the metadata-compatibility check applies only to that one shape.
fused-preattention-triton: writes q as [tokens, hq, d or 2d] contiguous, so a [B,1,...] view is free. No numerical interaction.
interference: C: No companion helps. The expected effect is below what one run, or a pair of runs, can resolve: LESSONS says identical code drifts 1.5-2.5% per shape, and the predicted change is <<1% on two sliding shapes weighted into a geomean of 12. An ab-revert of sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate would bring FA3 back on sliding decode_1, but that undoes a +25.6% win to measure a sub-1% knob and cannot change any decision. The only readable signal would be the FA3 kernel's own time in top_kernels on sliding decode_16/32, and FA3 rows are not shown to reproduce within the needed precision. With 2 attention checks left, the cost is not justified.
rules_flags: None substantive. Dropping cu_seqlens_q at L=1 is semantically identical: same keys, same precision, no host sync, no caching. Make sure the q_len==1 predicate stays config-only (it already is) and that the judge's scheduler_metadata, if still passed on full decode_1, is accepted with cu_seqlens_q=None. A mismatch would be a correctness failure, not a rules violation.
open_questions: If anyone wants the answer anyway, it can be settled for free without a check: read sgl_kernel/FA3 flash_api.cpp on a GPU-less clone to confirm is_varlen = ... || seqused_k.has_value(). If so, the hypothesis is a no-op at the template level and can be closed as moot.
Is fa3-scheduler-metadata-side-stream (running) going to change which path passes metadata on sliding decode_16/32? If it lands, any revisit of this idea should be re-based on it.
